entities.summary:
François-Marie, 1st duc de Broglie (1671–1745), emerged as a preeminent French military commander and diplomat during the early 18th century, a period defined by protracted dynastic conflicts and shifting European power balances. Elevated to Marshal of France in 1734 and granted the ducal title in 1742, Broglie's career spanned the reigns of Louis XIV and Louis XV, making him a central figure in the Bourbon monarchy's efforts to assert its dominance on the continent. His strategic acumen and battlefield leadership were instrumental in France’s military engagements across multiple theatres, solidifying his family’s position among the kingdom’s most distinguished noble houses.

Broglie's extensive military service commenced with the War of the Spanish Succession (1701–1714), where he distinguished himself at battles such as Malplaquet (1709) and Denain (1712), rising through the ranks from captain to lieutenant-general. Following a period of diplomatic service as ambassador to Great Britain from 1724 to 1727, he returned to active military command during the War of the Polish Succession (1733–1738), achieving notable victories in Italy at Parma and Guastalla (1734) and earning his marshal's bâton. His later career included commands in the War of the Austrian Succession (1740–1748), particularly in Bohemia, where he faced considerable challenges against Austrian forces.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: François-Marie de Broglie was a pivotal French military and diplomatic figure, serving three monarchs and significantly shaping France's role in major 18th-century European wars like the War of the Spanish and Polish Successions. His leadership contributed to key French military outcomes and solidified the ducal line of Broglie, a family that remained prominent in French history.

entities.summary:
François-Marie, 1st duc de Broglie (1671–1745), emerged as a pivotal military commander and diplomat during the waning years of Louis XIV's reign and the subsequent regency and reign of Louis XV. A scion of the Piedmontese House of Broglia, which had relocated to France, he distinguished himself through a career spanning nearly five decades, marked by service in major European conflicts from the War of the Spanish Succession to the War of the Austrian Succession. His strategic acumen and political astuteness positioned him as a key figure in the French military establishment, contributing significantly to France's geopolitical standing in Western Europe during a period of intense dynastic rivalries and shifting alliances.

Broglie's military career began in earnest during the War of the Spanish Succession (1701–1714), where he fought with distinction in numerous campaigns, earning promotion to Maréchal de camp by 1710. His service continued through the War of the Polish Succession (1733–1738), where he commanded French forces in Italy, notably leading the French to victory at the Battle of Crocetta in 1734. Elevated to Maréchal de France in 1734, he subsequently assumed command of the Army of Bohemia during the early stages of the War of the Austrian Succession (1740–1748), navigating complex logistical challenges and political pressures in Central Europe. Beyond his martial exploits, Broglie served as Governor of Strasbourg (1724–1728) and Languedoc (1728–1745), demonstrating administrative capability and securing his family's influence.
